QF.id: AIFM AIFs in India and Suitability_3

question.text: Lotus AIF is a Category III scheme with INR 300 crore of investible funds. The portfolio manager, Mr. Rohan Deshmukh, wants to take a concentrated long position in a single listed mid-cap stock. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the MAXIMUM rupee exposure this scheme can take in that single investee company?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that Category III AIFs cannot invest more than 10% of investable funds or NAV in a single investee company. 10% of INR 300 crore = INR 30 crore. Category I and Category II AIFs operate under a higher single-investee cap; Category III carries the tighter 10% limit, reflecting its leveraged and traded portfolio profile. The Trap: INR 75 crore (25%) is the higher Cat I/II-style limit and is the most tempting wrong answer if the candidate forgets that Cat III has a stricter cap. INR 15 crore (5%) and INR 100 crore (33%) are fabricated thresholds. Note: Remember the asymmetry — Category III carries the tighter 10% single-investee cap, while Category I and II AIFs work under a higher limit. Always apply the 10% to investable funds or NAV, not to committed capital.
